title: Finite-coefficient geometric-fiber formula
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be
geometric, and let $i_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$ and $a_{\bar y}:X_{\bar
y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ be the projections. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite
ring and let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The etale base-change morphism is
an isomorphism

$$
 \bar y^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Ra_{\bar y,*}i_{\bar y}^{-1}K.
$$

For a finite $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ this gives, for every $q\geq0$,

$$
 (R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 H^q(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}}).
$$

proof.text: Form the standard pullback of the proper morphism f along the geometric point y, with projections pullback.fst f y and pullback.snd f y. This supplies IsPullback.of_hasPullback f y and its commutative square, hence the specified derived exchange morphism.

A finite additive group is torsion, by Mathlib isAddTorsion_of_finite. The source-library moduleTorsionHomology_of_isTorsion therefore supplies torsion cohomology of every bounded-below complex of Lambda-module sheaves. Apply isIso_baseChange_of_isProper_of_torsionHomology, the module-valued form of bounded-below proper base change, to the square of step 1. This proves isIso_geometricFiber_finite without forgetting coefficients.

The module-valued identity-point germ is invertible. Apply the set-valued constancy and stalk theorem to the underlying sheaf. The module forgetful functor preserves the filtered colimit defining the stalk; its presheafFiberCompIso identifies the forgotten module germ with the set germ. It reflects isomorphisms, so the module germ is invertible. Compose its natural isomorphism with upperStarCompSheafFiberIso at y and the identity geometric point. Exactness of inverse image, via mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso, now identifies global sections of the source with the geometric stalk of higherDirectImage.

source.place: Tag 0DDF proof: pulling back by the geometric point produces the stalk; Tags 04JN and 04JQ

proof.text: The module clause of geometricPoint_pullback_stalk makes evaluation on the identity neighbourhood an equivalence. Transport across Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections: global sections on Spec Omega are exact. Use rightDerivedFunctorHomologyFunctorIso to commute global sections with cohomology. The natural isomorphism rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility identifies the bounded-below pushforward with the restriction of the unbounded one. The canonical generic module-valued Leray isomorphism rightDerivedLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso then identifies the target with cohomology on the geometric fibre. Finally mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor identify the pulled-back single complex with the single complex of the pulled-back sheaf. These are actual composed isomorphisms, with the prescribed endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0DDF(1) and SGA 4 XII Corollaire 5.2(iii): exact sections over the geometric point and Leray

proof.text: Apply the derived exchange theorem from step 2 to F placed in degree zero. Rewrite baseChange as derivedBaseChangeMapPlus. Mapping this isomorphism by the degree-q homology functor gives the specified baseChangeHomologyMap; global sections preserve its invertibility. Compose with the inverse source comparison from step 3 and target comparison from step 4. Isomorphisms compose, proving geometricFiber_finite_stalk_formula. No finiteness property of F is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DDF, lemma-proper-base-change-stalk, from Tag 0DDE; module-valued proper base change and the generic canonical Leray implementation in the source library. Lean proof by V1, 2026-10-18.

split_report.summary: Rewrote the one-line imported proof as six steps following Stacks Tag 0DDF (proper base change at a geometric stalk) and SGA 4 XII Cor. 5.2(iii). The blueprint proof specialized prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change, which is stated only for a torsion sheaf F, while the first formula is for complexes K in D^+(X_et, Lambda); the proof now uses thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below (Stacks 0DDE) directly, and prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change is no longer used. Hidden arguments made into new nodes: lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients (Lambda-linear exchange vs. the abelian one, Stacks 0D6J/07A7: the existing theorems are for abelian sheaves) and lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk (inverse image to Spec Omega is the stalk, Gamma(Spec Omega,-) an exact equivalence, Stacks 03Q1/04JN/04JQ). Torsionness of Lambda-module cohomology (n = #Lambda) and the derivation of the stalk formula (exactness of pullback and of Gamma on Spec Omega, Leray composition lem-kun-leray-bdd) are written out. stmt_deps: def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions replaced by the reviewed leaves def-weil-proper-morphism and def-weil-geometric-point, plus the notions the statement uses (fibre product, Lambda-module derived categories, exchange morphism, Rf_*, inverse image, stalk, etale cohomology). The hypothesis 'finite' on F is not used.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_geometricFiber_finite (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) : IsIso ((derivedBaseChangeMapPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f y).toCommSq).app K)
lean.note: Two clauses of the corollary: derived exchange and its cohomological geometric-stalk formula. The latter explicitly supplies endpoint comparison isomorphisms and transports the specified degree-q exchange map. Uses the existing finite-sheaf node def-constructible-finite, added to stmt_deps.
